# NCLEX Preparation Todo List

## **Foundation Setup (Weeks 1-2)**
- [ ] Register for the NCLEX with your state board of nursing
- [ ] Schedule your test date (give yourself 6-12 weeks to prepare)
- [ ] Purchase or access NCLEX prep materials (choose 1-2 primary resources)
- [ ] Create a dedicated study schedule (2-4 hours daily minimum)
- [ ] Set up a distraction-free study space

## **Content Review (Weeks 2-6)**
- [ ] Review all major content areas:
  - [ ] Safe and Effective Care Environment
  - [ ] Health Promotion and Maintenance
  - [ ] Psychosocial Integrity
  - [ ] Physiological Integrity
- [ ] Focus on weak areas identified in nursing school
- [ ] Master lab values and normal ranges
- [ ] Review pharmacology (drug classes, side effects, interactions)
- [ ] Study priority nursing frameworks (Maslow's, ABC's, safety)

## **Practice Questions (Daily)**
- [ ] Complete 75-150 practice questions per day
- [ ] Read ALL rationales (both correct and incorrect answers)
- [ ] Keep an error log of missed questions
- [ ] Focus on SATA (Select All That Apply) questions
- [ ] Practice prioritization and delegation questions

## **Test-Taking Strategies**
- [ ] Learn to identify key words in questions
- [ ] Practice the nursing process approach (ADPIE)
- [ ] Master elimination techniques
- [ ] Understand CAT (Computer Adaptive Testing) format
- [ ] Practice time management (1-2 minutes per question)

## **Final Week Preparation**
- [ ] Take a full-length practice exam
- [ ] Review error log and weak topics
- [ ] Confirm test center location and requirements
- [ ] Prepare required documents (ATT, ID)
- [ ] Plan test day logistics (transportation, arrival time)
- [ ] Reduce study intensity 1-2 days before exam
- [ ] Get adequate sleep (7-8 hours) before test day

## **Recommended Resources**
- [ ] Choose primary resource: UWorld, Kaplan, or ATI
- [ ] Supplement with: Mark Klimek lectures, NCLEX High Yield, or Simple Nursing
- [ ] Use NCSBN's free NCLEX review if needed

Remember: Consistency is key! Regular daily practice is more effective than cramming.
